thread:
maria_cs: FYI ACME says embeddings API p99 jumped to ~3s and some requests are timing out since 08:12 UTC. They sent a sample payload and logs.
liam_support: Ack, looking. Do you have the exact curl they used?
maria_cs: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.int/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{\n  \"model\": \"embed-lite-1\",\n  \"input\": "<large_text_sample>"\n}' — their payload was ~60KB.
ops-bot: ALERT: embeds.prod.p99_latency > 2.0s for tenant=acme (08:14:10 UTC) :warning:
liam_support: Ran a local repro with their sample. I see scheduler.queue_delay spiking to ~1.8s and worker_busy_count hitting capacity. Trace: https://traces.redwood/trace/abcd1234
anita_engineer: quick read — logs show tokenizer CPU spiking and worker threads busy during tokenization step. Long inputs cause blocking in preprocess stage, and admission controller queues up new requests behind it. Sample log: 
```
2026-03-17T08:13:52Z [embed-worker-7] preprocess: tokenization 3120ms input_len=61234 tenant=acme req_id=6f2a
2026-03-17T08:13:52Z [admission] queue_time_ms=1834 active_workers=32 tenant=acme
```
anita_engineer: This looks like a per-tenant hotspot from very large embed requests forcing sequential tokenization on worker threads. Not a model runtime p99 but admission/serialization backpressure.
liam_support: Confirmed: I reproduced and got 3.1s p99 when sending 60KB payloads; smaller payloads are fine.
anita_engineer: Mitigations (short-term):
- Apply per-tenant input_size cap (e.g., 32KB) for embeddings to reject or slow large requests.
- Increase acme's concurrency cap by +2 to reduce queueing while we patch.
- Enable tokenization offload flag for embed workers (threaded tokenization) in staging then prod.
Commands:
```
redwoodctl tenants update --id acme --max_input_size 32768
redwoodctl tenants update --id acme --concurrency 22
redwoodctl feature-flags set embed_tokenize_offload=true --env=prod
```
maria_cs: I'll tell the customer we're rate-limiting large inputs and ask them to resend as smaller batches.
ryan_oncall: I'm going to push the temp tenant cfg changes now (will stay for 2h). If the offload flag looks safe in staging, we'll roll to prod in 30m.
liam_support: Notifying ACME support contact: "We've applied a temporary input limit and bumped your concurrency; please retry and let us know if you still see timeouts." :thumbsup:
anita_engineer: Postmortem action items:
- Add targeted metric for tokenization latency (per-tenant).
- Add admission controller preemption: allow smaller requests to jump queue.
- Implement async tokenization in runtime to avoid blocking worker thread.
- Add a doc page for recommended input sizes per endpoint.
ryan_oncall: Change applied: increased concurrency + input cap. Monitoring now — p99 for tenant=acme dropped to 260ms within 90s.
liam_support: Customer confirmed reduced errors and lower latency. Closing for now; follow-up ticket created for the async tokenization work: CORE-9876.
maria_cs: Thanks team — I'll file the customer-facing note and update the case.
ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: embeds.p99_latency (tenant=acme). Duration: 00:09:12.
